blocker.summary: The r399 double-issue (this file's prior summary: sub_8236E868's size-1/size-256 requests returning the identical guest pointer 0x10082ab0) is RESOLVED, not just its own investigation continued. r413 traced it end to end: r366's own INVENTED fix for a real critical-section leak in sub_821FA9E0 (tools/apply_sub_821fa9e0_leave_fix.py) reused ctx.r3 -- which at that point already held sub_821FA9E0's own correct return value, reloaded two lines above -- to carry the RtlLeaveCriticalSection argument, and never restored it, so sub_821FA9E0 (the realloc() driving the C++ static-initializer growable array) always returned 0 whenever it had held the lock. That silently discarded every successful buffer growth, leaving the array's control block pointing at an already-freed buffer forever, which it then overflowed one word per registered static object (r410/r411), while a separate defect (r412: sub_821F90A8's capacity query deliberately returns -1 on a freed block, compared unsigned by the caller, so -1 reads as 'plenty of room') meant the array's own capacity check never re-fired to catch it. r414 applied a save/restore of ctx.r3 around r366's Leave call (new script tools/apply_sub_821fa9e0_leave_return_fix.py, r366's actual leak fix untouched) and verified live end to end (sub_821FA9E0/sub_823857E0/sub_8237FA50 now propagate the correct pointer; combined alloc/free event count on the same probe window jumped from 883 to 67239). r415 replayed r398's EXACT original repro unmodified against the fixed binary: all four previously-captured addresses are now distinct (deterministic, 2 launches) where two used to collide at 0x10082ab0 -- the actual symptom that opened this whole investigation is gone. r416 then checked the deeper success criterion this file previously named: sub_821D5F48 (which had never returned across sixteen prior allocator-subsystem findings) now RETURNS, and sub_821D7AE0/sub_821D7CD0 (the never-before-reached per-frame loop) are entered -- reproduced deterministically on 2 independent launches, same ~1.9s timing. NEW, NOT-YET-RESOLVED frontier named by r416: sub_821D7AE0/sub_821D7CD0 fire only TWICE, then the generated entry's own thread terminates itself (not a crash -- 'generated entry terminated its own thread') and presented_frames stays 0. Named for r417: read sub_821D7AE0/sub_821D7CD0 and their caller's PPC source to determine whether this two-pass-then-exit behavior is a normal, expected exit for a subsystem that is NOT actually 'the' presentation loop, or a new blocker cutting off a loop that should run indefinitely. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched -- reports and named tool scripts for r413/r414/r415/r416 were committed individually, the broader tree state was not.
